records.title: The largest theft in history: North Korea likely behind the $6.4 billion Binance hack — 05:00 UTC update
records.summary: Elliptic's 05:00 UTC update reports approximately $2.85B frozen or seized and $3.21B in assets outside issuer-freeze control at an approximately 04:30 UTC snapshot. The latter includes 233M XRP, 18,270 BTC, 519,104 ETH and approximately 475M TRX. XRP, SOL and NEAR had not moved as of that snapshot. Elliptic reports 434M USDT swapped for 160,451 ETH at a 12%-26% discount, a 59.9M USDT Aave collateral position against 44.2M debt with 19,762 ETH borrowed and near liquidation, 48M RLUSD sold before Ripple froze the remainder, an AVAX-to-USDC-to-CCTP-to-ETH route, a small Bitget laundering overlap, and likely TraderTraitor/DPRK attribution. No government attribution is confirmed.
records.methodology: Dated Elliptic article update and its stated on-chain holdings snapshot, swap/lending route reconstruction and attribution caveats.
records.limitations: The asset snapshot is approximately 04:30 UTC, not current at 10:45 UTC. Elliptic explicitly notes no official government attribution, a small Bitget overlap and atypically slow stablecoin conversion. CCTP use does not establish Circle knowledge or assistance.

records.title: Security Incident Update #2 (2026-10-30)
records.summary: Binance states that it allocated more than $6.34B in company funds, with $5B already held in the exact affected token assets, approximately $3B frozen on-chain, an initial PoR snapshot planned within 12 hours and results due by 2026-11-02. The 12-hour snapshot target was 2026-10-31 07:33 UTC and had elapsed by this retrieval; no public result was located in this check. The company does not disclose an XRP-specific replenishment allocation.
records.methodology: Official Binance Support announcement, published timestamp and stated restoration/PoR milestones.
records.limitations: Company statements are not an independent audit. No token-level XRP acquisition amount or completed XRP reserve crosswalk is disclosed.

records.title: Binance hack drained wallets backing customer assets, reserve data shows
records.summary: CoinDesk's review of Binance's October 1 PoR identifies Ethereum hot wallet Binance 14, reporting 89,475 ETH and 1.26B USDT in that snapshot. It estimates that approximately 204,500 ETH drained from Binance 14 and Binance 16 could reduce Binance's ETH backing near 94% until replenishment. CoinDesk says a November 1 reserve snapshot would show whether missing assets had been replaced. Binance 14 is an Ethereum wallet; this article does not crosswalk the five XRPL incident source wallets into Binance's XRP reserve set.
records.methodology: CoinDesk review of Binance's October 1 public PoR address data and Ethereum transaction records.
records.limitations: Secondary analysis, not a new Binance PoR or same-time customer-liability reconciliation. Binance14 evidence is Ethereum-specific and must not be extrapolated to XRP.

records.title: PR #1406 fixed-horizon outcome sampling integrity
records.summary: Fresh-main PR #1406 head 7e4cbbf045c667c2d03769cddd2501fdb04e10ef corrects the earlier ledger's acceptance of price observations up to 15 minutes after target_end. It resolves using the latest observation at or before the fixed horizon, rejects post-horizon and pre-issuance prices, requires outcome recording no earlier than target_end, and records effective horizon and pre-horizon observation lag. CI run 41193588765 passed 374 tests plus 8 subtests; fail-closed gate 41193588667 passed with merging disabled. PR remains draft, open and unmerged.
records.methodology: GitHub PR code diff, regression test log, exact-head CI and fail-closed gate.
records.limitations: This is a ledger and label-integrity foundation, not a trained model or walk-forward evaluation. Local OS file locking is not a distributed lock across independent runners. No forecast was issued.

records.methodology: GitHub PR diff, scheduler workflow source, queue readback, exact-head CI and gate logs.
records.limitations: Merging this proposal pauses scheduled queue execution until a durable external state store and narrowly scoped dispatch authorization are designed. It is not active on main.
